currentContext.expansion: DFPCL is in the final stages of a multi-year capex cycle, transitioning from capacity creation to commissioning during FY2026-27. Two flagship projects are underway: a greenfield 376 KTPA Technical Ammonium Nitrate (TAN) plant at Gopalpur, Odisha (95% complete, 10 million safe manhours achieved) and a brownfield Nitric Acid expansion at Dahej, Gujarat adding 300 KTPA Weak Nitric Acid and 150 KTPA Concentrated Nitric Acid capacity (86% complete, over five million safe manhours recorded); both are in pre-commissioning/commissioning stages with commissioning expected in H2 FY2026-27. risks.note: Reliance on imported phosphoric acid, potash, and ammonium sulphate exposes the Company to supply chain vulnerabilities and currency risks.

risks.risk: Working capital intensity and subsidy dependence
risks.note: The working capital-intensive nature of the business, coupled with dependence on government subsidies, poses liquidity and financial risks.
Risk of below-normal rains due to forecast El Nino impact, which can affect Crop Nutrition demand.
Evolving trade policies can impact overall supply chain economics and trade balance.
Risk of sudden policy changes affecting operations, such as subsidy levels, state incentives, export quotas and import duties.
Delay in passing increased raw material prices to end customers may impact the Company's margins and profitability.
Potential delays in regulatory clearances could affect timelines of capital projects such as the Gopalpur TAN plant and Dahej Nitric Acid expansion.
Absence of natural hedges exposes the business to forex fluctuations.

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.

themes.title: Fertilizer subsidy & nutrient-policy cycle
themes.need: Fertilizer makers are driven by NBS/urea subsidy policy, gas-pooling and nutrient pricing rather than the crop-protection volume/molecule-launch recovery. Q1FY27's supply-side read comes from MBAPL: revenue roughly flat at INR 416cr with EBITDA +16% and PAT +17% purely on cheap March-bought raw material that management said is now EXHAUSTED, with utilisation only ~43-45% because of raw-material availability rather than demand - SSP sales were +28% and NPK +33% YoY against production down 7%/28%. Its Dhule (Maharashtra) integrated complex commissions +3,30,000 MTPA DAP-NPK plus 99,000 MTPA phosphoric acid in Oct-2026 and a second phase in Oct-2027, framed as a >50% turnover jump toward ~INR 3,500cr revenue and 15.6 lakh MT capacity by FY28; Egypt/Jordan rock-phosphate sourcing (non-Hormuz) insulated it relative to import-dependent peers. Subsidy clarity and gas costs still set the near-term margin.
themes.driver: NBS/urea subsidy policy (the Oct-Mar rate revision), gas-pooling and nutrient pricing; MBAPL's Oct-2026 Dhule commissioning and the utilisation ramp toward ~90%; kharif demand pull-through after a delayed monsoon.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: DFPCL is a diversified, multi-product organisation serving critical sectors of the Indian economy including mining, pharma & chemicals, infrastructure, and agriculture. It operates across four strategic business verticals - Industrial Chemicals, Mining Chemicals, Crop Nutrition Business and Value-Added Real Estate - with manufacturing facilities at Taloja, Dahej, Srikakulam, and Panipat, and a new facility at Gopalpur nearing completion. Following a strategic restructuring, Industrial Chemicals and Value-Added Real Estate sit under DFPCL itself, Mining Chemicals under Deepak Mining Solutions Limited (DMSL), and Crop Nutrition under Mahadhan AgriTech Limited (MAL).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Industrial/Pharma Chemicals outlook is guardedly positive: raw material and energy cost volatility and feedstock availability concerns may persist given geo-political scenarios, but strong demand is expected for Nitric Acid and Iso Propyl Alcohol on favourable growth in downstream pharma, agri, industrial manufacturing and mining
- A steadily expanding specialty chemicals portfolio continues to gain traction with key accounts, enhancing the resilience and relevance of the overall Industrial Chemicals business mix
- Mining Chemicals growth momentum is expected to continue, supported by government thrust on construction, power and infrastructure development, with resulting uptick in explosives demand across mining and infrastructure benefiting the TAN and Explosives growth strategy
- Mining Chemicals sales volumes grew 11% in FY2025-26, driven by robust B2C demand and improved customer engagement
- Crop Nutrition outlook is cautiously optimistic despite the possibility of a slightly below-normal monsoon influenced by El Nino; long-term demand is supported by increasing focus on crop productivity, balanced nutrition and soil health, with the Company prioritising key crops and expanding in irrigated and high-value segments
- Specialty and Croptek products contributed 33% of Crop Nutrition revenues, reflecting continued focus on differentiated and value-added offerings
- FY2025-26 profitability was impacted by elevated input costs, pricing pressures in Industrial Chemicals, limited subsidy realignment in fertilisers, and planned ammonia plant turnaround activities, partly offset by lower finance costs and operational discipline
- With improving market conditions and the two key growth projects (Gopalpur TAN, Dahej Nitric Acid) nearing completion, the Company sees itself as well-positioned for sustainable growth and long-term value creation

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: DFPCL is in the final stages of a multi-year capex cycle, transitioning from capacity creation to commissioning during FY2026-27. Two flagship projects are underway: a greenfield 376 KTPA Technical Ammonium Nitrate (TAN) plant at Gopalpur, Odisha (95% complete, 10 million safe manhours achieved) and a brownfield Nitric Acid expansion at Dahej, Gujarat adding 300 KTPA Weak Nitric Acid and 150 KTPA Concentrated Nitric Acid capacity (86% complete, over five million safe manhours recorded); both are in pre-commissioning/commissioning stages with commissioning expected in H2 FY2026-27. Separately, DMSL had already expanded its existing TAN capacity from 487 KTPA to 587 KTPA over the prior two years through brownfield expansion. DMSL continues strategic investment in forward integration into commercial explosives and initiating systems, and in Bulk-Mix-Delivery (BMD) trucks for down-the-hole ANFO delivery, to support its Total Cost of Ownership model. PCL's 1,500 TPD greenfield Ammonia plant produced 452 KT of ammonia in FY2025-26, meeting around 93% of the Group's ammonia requirement. In Crop Nutrition, the Company established a DSIR-accredited Research and Innovation Centre (RIC) at Pune, and in Value-Added Real Estate, Creaticity added new furniture/home-decor brands (Trezure Casa, Houslife, Edo Homes, Sleepy Cat, Morning Owl, Boingg Kids Furniture) plus fulfilment centres and a sports arena (Serve Society's Pickle and Padel courts) during the year.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leadership in both the solvent (IPA) and acid (Nitric Acid) segments of Industrial Chemicals
- Around 45% share in India's merchant Nitric Acid market, supported by captive consumption for TAN and Ammonium Nitro Phosphate production
- Leading position in India's Technical Ammonium Nitrate (TAN) market with an estimated ~40% market share; highest-ever TAN sales volume of 577 KT in FY2025-26 (up 11% YoY)
- Multi-location acid production facilities provide a supply-chain edge, especially serving major consumers in West and Central India
- Broad distribution network: 250+ channel partners and nearly 1,000 direct customers across 28 states/UTs, exporting to 23 countries
- Proprietary Nutrient Unlock Technology (NUT) in Crop Nutrition, differentiating Mahadhan's fertilisers via enhanced nutrient use efficiency
- Leadership position in water-soluble fertilisers in India, with strong presence in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka
- Backward integration across LNG-Ammonia-Nitric Acid-downstream value chain, reinforced by a long-term LNG supply agreement with Equinor, described as difficult to replicate
- PCL's captive ammonia production meets around 93% of the Group's ammonia requirement, with PCL also holding ~33% merchant ammonia market share in western India
- Post commissioning of the Dahej Nitric Acid expansion, DFPCL is positioned to become Asia's largest Nitric Acid producer

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] Deck shows "Corporate Structure post Demerger" with DFPCL and MAL, listing Mining Chemicals (TAN), Crop Nutrition, Industrial Chemicals, Value Added Real Estate (VARE), Ammonia, subsidiaries CCPL (mining explosives) and DGCPL (LNG trading), plus blasting services in Australia; the deck does not explain the demerger terms.
- [Regulation - PESO] TAN production and dispatch were disrupted by "PESO ANRS portal changes", the stated reason for the 12% YoY volume decline.
- [Regulation - RGP quota] Government of India curtailed the RGP quota (linked by the deck to the US-Iran conflict), cutting IPA volumes 76% YoY and forcing a shutdown; outlook says relaxation of the quota improves supply availability "however, correction in domestic IPA prices is expected".
- [Demand outlook] Monsoon-driven slowdown in mining/infrastructure may hit Q2 TAN demand though elevated FGAN prices should support margin; for Crop Nutrition, El Nino impact expected to be limited with "only 12 of 44 core districts likely to receive below-normal rainfall".
- [Gas] Margin support attributed to an Equinor gas arrangement; the deck gives no contract volume, tenure or pricing.
